# Govern Business Requirements

## Supplied BRD and Technical Intent

Use this path when the user supplies an existing BRD, Technical Intent, or both. Load the supplied direction before considering new-document authoring or an unanswered full questionnaire. The graphical wizard is optional; an external agent uses the same CIS services through the CLI.

Read `.cis/workspace.yml` and identify its product-owned authority repository. If setup is missing, follow `cis-repository-bootstrap`; retain the maintainer-selected documentation root and normal confirmation controls. Locate the installed `cis` command or the launcher documented by that repository. Check `cis definition documents --help`, `cis definition prepare --help`, and `cis definition status --help` for the delivered version.

Replace the quoted placeholders below with actual values: `<workspace>` is the directory containing `.cis/workspace.yml`; source placeholders are absolute paths to the supplied Markdown files. Load only the supplied roles; a missing role uses its existing governed document or remains a reported prerequisite. CIS copies external source files into the project and preserves the originals.

Use argument-list process APIs where available. Otherwise follow the active shell's literal-argument quoting rules for paths and authorised text. Never interpolate document contents into command text. Serialize multiline technical-decision resolutions into a UTF-8 JSON file and pass its path through `--input`.

```sh
cis definition documents --workspace "<workspace>" --role business --source "<absolute-brd.md>" --format json
cis definition documents --workspace "<workspace>" --role technical --source "<absolute-technical-intent.md>" --format json
cis graph build --workspace "<workspace>" --format json
cis definition prepare --workspace "<workspace>" --page technical --format json
cis definition status --workspace "<workspace>" --format json
```

For a document already inside the project, use `definition documents --role <role> --path "<repository-relative-path>"` with the same workspace and JSON options instead of `--source`. Selecting a file and preparing technical direction are domain actions; no prior GUI visit or display-page navigation is required. `definition init` is available to start or resume the domain session, but is not a prerequisite for these commands.

Inspect `errors`, `warnings`, `pages` and their `complete`/`current`/`issues` fields, `technicalQuestions.questions`, and `readyToActivate`. A successful command can return exit code zero while review or adoption remains incomplete. Source-derived fields retain `resolutionSource` and `evidence`: `selected-document` is working direction pending baseline adoption; `accepted-document` is accepted source authority. The coordinator's `definition status` is the working-draft projection. A direct `technical-intent questions status` outside setup can intentionally show unadopted source passages as suggestions; this does not create a need to transcribe them again.

Reuse supplied requirements and settled facts, including supported prose, lists, tables and identified headings. CIS owns interpretation and stable internal identities; the ordinary load path does not require a layout-mapping JSON file or a rewritten source. Treat an import diagnostic as an affected-source problem, a contradiction as a focused conflict retaining both sources, and only a necessary unresolved decision as a question. Preserve other resolved fields. Optional scope marked `Not requested` records neither an exclusion nor an invented implementation choice.

For a genuinely unresolved technical item, use the [authorised-answer procedure](../cis-govern-technical-intent/SKILL.md#supplied-direction-and-authorised-answers). Read its current context and revision token where provided, obtain the user's actual decision, and save only that explicitly authorised answer. An actor name is provenance, not permission to decide. Baseline adoption and approval remain explicit governed actions; loading or preparing inputs grants no approval.

Resume from a new agent process with `cis definition status --workspace "<workspace>" --format json`, then repeat `definition prepare --page technical` when its diagnostics require reconciliation. Read and update state through CIS operations; preserve source files, managed metadata, approval hashes and recorded decisions.

## Workflow

1. Confirm `.cis/workspace.yml` identifies one product, one ecosystem, and exactly one product-owned `authority` repository. If not, dry-run `cis workspace init --root <documentation-root> --ecosystem <id> --product <id>` and request review before using `--yes`.
2. Run `cis graph build --workspace <workspace>` and `cis graph status --workspace <workspace>` before intake. Reserve `cis graph validate --workspace <workspace>` for deep structural assurance.
3. Run `cis brd discover --workspace <workspace> --format agent`. Treat every found BRD, product-design document such as a GDD, or feature specification in product-owned repositories as unverified source evidence; absence creates no implied requirements. Exclude dependency repositories because their requirements belong to another product authority.
4. For a supplied BRD, use the supplied-input path above and inspect its interpretation. Run `cis brd init --workspace <workspace> --title <title>` only when a genuinely new canonical BRD is required. Preserve the authority repository's document, narrative, stable identities and catalog entry. Existing `cis brd layout` remains an advanced diagnostic for an explicit unsupported mapping case; it is not the ordinary import prerequisite. Keep Open questions in its existing answer workflow and preserve genuine unresolved decisions.
5. After implementation graph rebuilds, run `cis technical-intent refresh --workspace <workspace> --format agent` before starting the next feature. Do not request renewed BRD, technical-intent, or backlog approval when this safe refresh succeeds. If its BRD stage blocks on new or materially changed source evidence, use `cis brd reconcile --workspace <workspace> --format agent`, review the exact semantic delta, and request only the authority that delta requires.
6. Review every source row. Set Assessment to `Adopted`, `Reference`, or `Rejected` and record rationale. For an Adopted feature specification, incorporate its business intent into the relevant BRD sections and cite its `BRD-SRC-*` ID in Traceability.
7. When an agent drafted the BRD and another review-capable provider is available, run `cis agent review brd --provider <different-provider> --actor <human>`. Include extracted authoring evidence only with explicit disclosure authority. Treat the structured findings as advisory evidence, never approval or stakeholder answers.
8. If the review contains findings, run `cis brd review init <review-run-id>`. Present the complete recommendation list together. Let the human approve items as written, provide exact edited remediation text through `cis brd review decide`, or approve every unchanged pending item atomically with `cis brd review accept-all`; do not invent a separate acceptance rationale or aggregate approval. Previously edited approvals must survive the batch action. Completion mechanically locks the exact set. Use `cis brd review approve` only to recover a complete legacy set that predates automatic locking.
9. Apply an approved recommendation set with `cis agent revise brd --review <review-run-id> --provider <provider-different-from-reviewer> --actor <human>`. The isolated agent must apply exactly the approved identities and recommendation text, preserve legacy rejected findings as guardrails, and change only the BRD. Preserve source identity, path, hash, assessment, ordering, and provenance; source rationale may change only when an approved recommendation explicitly requires it. If deterministic copy-back rejects an otherwise successful retained revision, correct the gate/candidate and repeat the same command so CIS revalidates that run without another provider execution. Then run `cis agent review brd` with a provider different from the reviser for closure-only verification. That pass may report only missed accepted scope, introduced rejected scope, revision-caused regressions, or protected evidence/scope drift; do not reopen broad completeness or unrelated refinement.
10. Run `cis brd questions guidance` and present the complete question list with its bounded BRD context. `cis brd questions suggest` may create local, digest-bound advisory answers; use a remote provider only after explicit disclosure authority. Present an answer as supported only when it has at least medium model confidence and cites the displayed context; low-confidence, uncited, malformed, or insufficient output must remain absent. Record only a suggestion explicitly accepted by the human or the human's edited text with `cis brd questions answer <id> --answer <answer> --actor <human>`. Never treat generation as acceptance or infer a missing stakeholder decision. Partial progress may be preserved. After each answer, use `cis brd review freshness <review-run-id>`: `question-answers-only` remains compatible while resolution is incomplete; `stale` requires another review.
11. Once every question is answered, run `cis agent incorporate brd-questions --provider <implement-provider> --actor <human>`. Bind the exact answer digest and identities, preserve the canonical question table and managed evidence, and reflect the decisions in relevant business sections without inventing technical choices or scope. Then run `cis agent review brd` through a provider different from the question reviser. That closure pass checks only missed or incorrect incorporation and concrete regressions. Never route directly from completed answers to approval.
12. Rebuild workspace graphs after canonical edits, then run `cis brd validate` and `cis brd status`.
13. Present validation errors, warnings, participant baseline drift, unresolved sources, unanswered questions, independent-review findings, and approval readiness to the user.
14. Run `cis brd approve --reviewer <human> --reason <rationale>` only after the user explicitly authorizes that exact approval. Rebuild the authority graph after approval.
15. After technical intent is Active/current, run `cis solution-design init`. Review and approve the overall architecture and component sheet as one bundle.
16. After the solution-design bundle is Active/current, capture and approve high-level UI direction through `cis ui-direction questions init`, `cis ui-direction init`, validation, and explicit human approval. Then run `cis brd backlog build`. Consume CIS's effective requirement interpretation, including supported canonical tables, prose, plain or numbered bullets, unbolded identified paragraphs and identified headings. Preserve existing identities and CIS-generated stable identities; presentation changes do not create new business decisions. Follow the existing source-version adoption controls. Route only to product-owned participants, or to the authority when it is the sole owned greenfield repository. Never route implementation to a dependency. Review functional-requirement coverage, repository routing, frontend types, dependencies, and global obligations, then validate and present approval readiness.
17. Run `cis brd backlog approve --reviewer <human> --reason <rationale>` only with explicit authority. An approved high-level item may then become a feature specification; it is not an implementation task.
18. Start only a dependency-ready item with `cis brd backlog start --item <HLT-ID>`. Complete the generated Draft specification and run `cis brd feature validate --item <HLT-ID>` until it is Ready for Approval.
19. Present the exact feature scope, validation result, and approval rationale. Run `cis brd feature approve --item <HLT-ID> --reviewer <human> --reason <rationale>` only with explicit human authority.
20. After feature approval, rebuild the graph and reconcile the now-eligible feature evidence into the BRD. Use `cis technical-intent refresh`; renew downstream authority only when it reports an actual semantic change. In the VS Code delivery loop these mechanical steps, feature-rooted change creation, deterministic impact analysis, and `cis plan derive` are one continuation after approval; do not send an unchanged BRD back through secondary review merely because the approved feature was added to managed traceability.

## Guardrails

Never infer currency from file existence, choose source or review-finding dispositions, claim semantic absorption without updating BRD content and traceability, invent business requirements, approve on a user's behalf, or describe Review Required, Ready for Approval, or Stale content as Active. Agents cannot accept, reject, or approve review findings. Answer completion alone is not approval-ready: governed answers must be incorporated and independently reviewed. Do not edit managed candidate IDs, approval hashes, source hashes, baseline rows, review-disposition blocks, or block markers. CIS may mark an approved BRD, backlog, or feature Stale from content/evidence drift; only explicit human approval may restore Active status. Feature approval accepts scope but never authorizes implementation.

## Human-readable content

Apply the [shared content standard](../../../docs/standards/human-readable-content-standard.md) to in-scope prose. Use [cis-technical-writing](../cis-technical-writing/SKILL.md) for documents and reports, [cis-ux-writing](../cis-ux-writing/SKILL.md) for interface wording, and [cis-content-review](../cis-content-review/SKILL.md) for source-aware review followed by a separate reader check. Preserve this workflow's authority, evidence, privacy and lifecycle rules. Clarity does not remove legitimate uncertainty or mandatory specification sections.
